<span id="what-it-is"></span>
== What it is ==

An agent behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (an <code>adk serve</code> agent, llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, a gateway) becomes a Discord bot with slash commands, per-server [[Company Brain/Plugins and packs|plugins]], rate limits, and [[Company Brain/Approvals|approval buttons]] only operators can press.

<span id="setup"></span>
== Setup ==

<syntaxhighlight lang="bash">pip install "awdiscord[gateway]"
awdiscord setup
awdiscord run</syntaxhighlight>
You create the application yourself at the Discord developer portal and paste the bot token once. <code>setup</code> does the rest. Walk-through: [[Company Brain/Guide: setting up your company brain in Discord|Guide: company brain in Discord]].

<span id="what-you-get"></span>
== What you get ==

* Slash commands: see the [[Company Brain/Discord command reference|command reference]]
* Built-in plugins: community, projects, github, hub, join
* Voice calls with notes, summaries and action items
* [[Company Brain/Bring your own model|Bring your own model]] per server with <code>/model</code>
* A local inbox for approvals and notifications from your own code
* [[Company Brain/Safety rails|Safety rails]]

<span id="configuration"></span>
== Configuration ==

See [[Company Brain/awdiscord configuration variables|awdiscord configuration variables]].

<span id="running-under-a-supervisor"></span>
== Running under a supervisor ==

<code>awdiscord run --inbox-port 8371</code> opens <code>GET /health</code>. The awdk addon manifest uses it, so <code>adk addon</code> can start, health-check and restart the bot.
